title: Collective thermalization, work reliability, and resource bounds in a population-inverted Dicke Otto engine
authors: Cler T. Garcez, Gabriella G. Damas, Norton G. de Almeida, G. D. de Moraes Neto
abstract: Population inversion and collective relaxation can both enhance the performance of a quantum heat engine, but through distinct mechanisms. We study a quantum Otto engine whose working medium is a symmetric collective spin of $N$ two-level constituents. For commuting work strokes and collective reservoir coupling, the dynamics reduces exactly to a finite birth--death process on the Dicke ladder, allowing a unified treatment of stationary operation, work fluctuations, and finite-time relaxation. In the complete-reset limit, passive work per cycle saturates with system size, whereas population inversion yields work that grows linearly with $N$. The work reliability shows the same linear scaling, exceeding the square-root behavior of $N$ independent engines. This enhancement originates from a macroscopic polarization displacement between hot and cold states, while collective coupling instead accelerates the finite-time dynamics through Dicke transition rates. For matched passive and inverted hot states, the extra gross work equals the Otto efficiency times the ergotropy of the inverted state. Charging the corresponding reversible excess state-formation cost removes this advantage, showing that the enhanced output converts a pre-existing active-state resource rather than generating a free thermodynamic gain. Exact finite-contact trajectory statistics further quantify how collective kinetics, fluctuations, correlations, and resource accounting remain linked away from complete reset.
summary: This work analyzes a quantum Otto engine using a collective spin model, showing that population inversion leads to super-classical scaling of work and reliability with system size N. The authors rigorously prove that this enhanced work is not a free thermodynamic gain but rather the conversion of an existing active resource. The methodology relies on mapping the dynamics to a finite birth-death process for exact statistical treatment.
main_problem: The paper aims to disentangle the distinct contributions of population inversion and collective coupling to the performance and reliability of a quantum Otto engine.
main_result: Population inversion allows the extracted work and work reliability to scale linearly with system size N, significantly exceeding the scaling of independent engines. However, this enhancement is shown to convert a pre-existing active resource rather than generating free energy.
method: The dynamics are modeled as a finite birth-death process on the Dicke ladder, allowing for the unified treatment of mean work, fluctuations, and resource accounting.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum Otto engine whose working medium is a symmetric collective spin of N two-level constituents, described by the Dicke model sector. The cycle involves work strokes (isochores) and hot/cold reservoir contacts governed by a collective Davies-form generator.
key_observables: Mean extracted work, work fluctuations, work reliability, and ergotropy.
important_parameters: System size N, temperature parameters (related to reservoir coupling), and the degree of population inversion.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes commuting work strokes and collective reservoir coupling; the resource analysis requires careful accounting of state-formation costs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the four-stroke collective Otto cycle, detailing the sequence of state changes between work strokes and reservoir contacts.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the model and cycle, then analyzing the complete-reset limit for work and reliability, followed by a detailed resource accounting section, and concluding with an analysis of finite-contact trajectory statistics.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantitative framework for analyzing non-equilibrium thermodynamics in many-body quantum systems, specifically quantifying how collective quantum correlations enhance energy extraction beyond classical limits.
